newsitem.title: UK: UK judge tells bomb case jury to avoid Mideast talk.
newsitem.headline: UK judge tells bomb case jury to avoid Mideast talk.

text.p: A jury selected to try four people over a bomb attack on the Israeli embassy in London was told on Tuesday to avoid discussions about the Middle East conflict during the trial.
"This is a high profile case. It starts with two car bombs - one outside the Israeli Embassy and the other outside a Jewish philanthropic institution," Judge Patrick Garland told the jury.

"Due to current problems in the Middle East, it is very much in the public eye...Do not allow people to talk to you about this case or about the Palestine situation or about the Israeli state," he added.
The trial is expected to start on Wednesday of two men and two women defendants of Palestinian origin on charges of conspiring to cause explosions between January 1993 and May 1995.
The four, who all deny the charges, were arrested after blasts at the Israeli embassy in July 1994 and at a Jewish fund-raising centre in London the same day.
Judge Garland told the jurors they would not have to enter court through the main fron door and would be given their own dining facilities.
